name: Manchester Metropolitan University

settingEvidence.evidence: our city-centre campus puts you right at the heart of it

fees.text: £10,050 per year for UK students on standard full-time courses starting in 2027 (2027/28). Manchester Met says 2027/28 tuition fees are still being finalised and may change; its course pages show the Home fee as 'to be confirmed'.

source.evidence: The standard UK and Channel Islands full-time fee will be £10,050 in academic year 2027/28.

livingCosts.text: Halls cost about £160-£245 a week depending on the hall and room (2026/27 prices, covering Manchester Met and partner halls). The weekly fee is paid for the length of the contract.

source.evidence: Prices shown are for the academic year 2026/27. Prices represent the weekly fee and are for the length

contextual.summary: Manchester Met does not publish contextual (lower) offers or criteria. It says it will consider challenges you tell it about, plus contextual data it holds on applicants, at the confirmation stage and may make allowances then.
contextual.rulesText: Admissions page: the university will consider any issues it is made aware of, as well as the contextual data it has on applicants, at the confirmation phase and may make allowances at that point. Applicants and offer holders who want an issue considered should contact the relevant admissions team.

source.evidence: We will consider any issues we are made aware of, as well as the contextual data we have on applicants, at the confirmation phase of the admissions process and may make allowances at this point.

programmes.name: First Generation Scholarship programme
programmes.summary: Support programme for Year 12 and 13 students in the North West whose parents did not go to university, with an on-campus summer taster, development sessions and a £1,500 scholarship if you later study a full-time undergraduate degree at Manchester Met.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 students at a state-maintained post-16 institution who live or study in the North West (Lancashire, Cumbria, Cheshire, Merseyside or Greater Manchester), are UK home students, went to a UK state high school, and whose parents or guardians did not go to university.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Be in Year 12 at a state-maintained post-16 institution; be a home (UK) student; live or study in the North West (Lancashire, Cumbria, Cheshire, Merseyside, Greater Manchester); have attended a UK state high school; be studying a two-year Level 3 qualification (A levels or BTECs); neither parent or guardian has an undergraduate degree (does not apply to care leavers); at least six GCSEs at grades 9-4 including English language and maths. If the programme is oversubscribed, priority goes to applicants who are or have been looked after, are estranged from their families, are from military families, or live in a low-participation neighbourhood (lowest POLAR4 quintile). Exceptions may be made for individual circumstances.
benefits: Place on the First Generation Summer University Taster, an on-campus event (online options for those living further away)
Development sessions on personal statements, time management, motivation, exams and revision, student finance and budgeting, and confidence
Pre-entry guidance for your university application and networking with current students with similar life experience
£1,500 First Generation scholarship if you go on to a full-time undergraduate degree at Manchester Met
You do not have to apply to Manchester Met to take part in the pre-entry phase
